approachQuestion.prompt:
Count rectangular mount frames

Input: records (y,x1,x2), each describing exactly two mounting points (x1,y) and (x2,y) on one horizontal row. All y values are distinct and x1≠x2 in every record. There are no other points. Return the number of nondegenerate axis-aligned rectangles whose four corners are supplied mounting points. Coordinate order within a row is arbitrary.

Example 1: rows = [(1,2,8),(4,8,2),(7,2,8),(9,2,6)]. Output: 3, from choosing two of the first three rows. Example 2: rows = [(0,1,4),(3,1,5)]. Output: 0. Example 3: rows = []. Output: 0. 0 ≤ n ≤ 200,000; the answer fits signed 64-bit arithmetic.

Constraints: input is immutable; all identifiers and numeric entries are signed 32-bit integers unless specified. Arithmetic uses signed 64-bit integers. Prefer the least expected running-time growth, then avoid unnecessary asymptotic auxiliary storage. Non-adversarial hashing of fixed-size integer keys/tuples has expected amortized constant cost.

options.text: Normalize each row’s two x coordinates to (min,max). Keep prior frequencies of those pairs; add the current pair’s prior frequency to the rectangle total, then increment it.
options.feedback: A rectangle needs two distinct rows with the same two x coordinates. Every row has exactly two points, so matching normalized pairs is necessary and sufficient.

options.text: Normalize all pairs, build their final frequencies, then sum c(c−1)/2 over frequency entries c.
options.feedback: Every unordered pair of rows within a signature class forms exactly one rectangle. This gives equivalent time and auxiliary-space growth.

options.text: Compare every pair of rows and test whether their normalized x pairs match.
options.feedback: This is correct but brute force: it repeats comparisons against all earlier rows even though matching signatures can be counted directly.

options.text: Group rows only by the horizontal width |x2−x1| and count row pairs within each width.
options.feedback: Rows (0,1,4) and (3,2,5) have equal widths but no shared pair of vertical sides, so they form no rectangle.

feedback.reason: Reduce a geometric counting condition to equality of a complete normalized row signature.
details: Scan the row records without sorting them. Normalize the two x coordinates into an integer-pair key. Add its prior frequency to a 64-bit rectangle total, then increment its frequency in a map.

Two distinct rows form a rectangle exactly when both normalized x coordinates match. Equal widths at shifted positions are insufficient. Adding the prior frequency counts every new row-pair without listing rectangles.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Count rectangular mount frames — analyzed method”, n is the number of row records and u is the number of distinct normalized x-coordinate pairs. Choose its time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input for the stated size parameters, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.

feedback.reason: One normalized-pair lookup counts potentially many rectangles at once.
details: Reduce a geometric counting condition to equality of a complete normalized row signature.
Each row uses constant-size normalization, expected constant-cost map operations and one scalar addition. Counting many rectangles numerically does not require listing them: expected O(n+1).
O(u+1) for distinct normalized x pairs and counters. Supplied row records and the scalar result are excluded.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(u + 1) auxiliary space.”: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hashing model.
“Expected O(n² + 1) time; O(u + 1) space.”: The potentially quadratic number of rectangles is accumulated as counts; rectangles are not enumerated.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(1) space.”: The map retains one count for each of u distinct x-coordinate pairs.
“Expected O(n log n + 1) time; O(n + 1) space.”: Only each pair of endpoints is normalized; all rows are not sorted.
